Title: Diagnosis of test `org.apache.commons.csv.CSVRecordTest.testToMapWithNoHeader()`

Details: The test `testToMapWithNoHeader` creates a CSV parser with the input "a,b" and a CSV format defined by `CSVFormat.newFormat(',')` which does not specify headers. It obtains the first record and calls `toMap()` on it. 

From investigation, `CSVRecord.toMap()` invokes `putIn(new HashMap<>(values.length))`. The `putIn` method iterates over the `mapping` field's entries to map column names to values by column index.

The crucial part is how `mapping` is initialized in `CSVRecord`. This `mapping` is created by the parser and passed at record creation. The parser's constructor calls `initializeHeader()` to set up `headerMap` (later passed as `mapping`).

`initializeHeader()` returns null if no header information is provided or read. It checks if `format.getHeader()` is null; if it is, it returns null header map. If the header array is empty, it tries to read the first record as header. 

In the test case, the format's header is likely null and the input "a,b" with no explicit header means `headerMap` is null.

When `mapping` is null in the `CSVRecord`, the `putIn` method will throw a `NullPointerException` when it tries to iterate over `mapping.entrySet()`. This causes test failure.

Hence the root cause is that `CSVRecord.toMap()` does not handle the case where there is no header (mapping is null). It assumes a header mapping is always present but in the test scenario, no header exists, so `mapping` is null, causing NPE.

Suggested fix: Methods related to `CSVRecord.toMap` or `CSVRecord.putIn`, or the way `CSVRecord.mapping` is handled should be adjusted to safely handle null mapping or provide an empty map to avoid NPE when no header is present.

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
